findings.finding: Inspected Thomas Tatton’s primary technical account, printed pp11–12. He specifies excellent performers throughout, an extremely high first viola, sixth-viola C string lowered to B-flat, exposed one/two melodic parts over accompaniment, and substantial ensemble difficulty. This is technical testimony, not inspected notation.

grade.basis: Informed testimony-based diploma estimate: the extreme upper register and exposed melodic delivery put the first viola beyond routine advanced playing; the six-part balance, intonation and scordatura demand mature ensemble control. Tatton’s own reluctance to assemble an unrehearsed performance supports substantial rehearsal demands. No score preview was inspected, so exact range, passage density and any professional-level ceiling remain unverified; level 7 is a cautious whole-work assessment, not a claim to have read the score.

findings.finding: Inspected all 13 PDF pages: three complete seven-page parts in imposed spreads plus cover. Violin 1 finale printed p6 has explicit 5te and 6te position indications in the repeated passage after D; p7 around L–M and R includes upper-register runs and another 6te Pos. indication. Other movements contain chromatic runs, shifts and double stops; violin 2 and violin 3 were also read in full.

grade.basis: Complete original edition, all four pieces and all three parts inspected. Violin 1 sets an advanced/ABRSM8 floor through recurring upper-position playing reaching explicit sixth position, rapid slurred scale figures, chromatic intonation, string-crossing arpeggios and double stops. The finale printed pp6–7 is a recurring demand, not an isolated high note. Violin 2 also has active runs and chords; violin 3 supplies mobile bass and double-stop support. Standard metres and mostly regular textures keep ensemble coordination within this level; no extra level is warranted.

findings.finding: Inspected the complete eight-page Steve Jones arrangement through final bar157. All five staves use alto clef, although the full score retains violin/viola/cello template labels. Chromatic central writing occurs in bars39–57 and122–134; triplet accompaniment and a 3/4 section occur bars74–89; wide register changes and sustained exposed upper lines recur.
Inspected separate part title and notation: explicitly Viola 1, corresponding to the top score staff and its high sustained vocal melody.

Inspected separate part title and notation: explicitly Viola 3, corresponding to score staff3; recurring wide ascending slurs, upper-register melody and chromatic inner-line movement provide a comparable secondary challenge.

grade.basis: Exact five-viola Jones version, complete score inspected. First viola’s exposed sustained upper-register melody requires secure shifting, soft entries and long-bow control; viola3 has more continuous movement, broad slurred changes of register and chromatic inflection. The Andante pace, predominantly single-note writing and limited fast passagework make early advanced/ABRSM7 a proportionate whole-work level. Five-player balance, chromatic tuning and maintaining the lullaby pulse beneath the changing melodic emphasis require rehearsal but do not justify an additional level.
